title: Copilot Studio: persistent identity (agent accounts) for agents
summary: Hold: the statement that Microsoft Learn names no roles for the Power Platform administration step is too broad. Microsoft documents Power Platform administrative roles that manage environments and settings; the roadmap facts, preview licensing, activation and blocking controls otherwise match the sources checked.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio makers can give agents their own persistent Microsoft 365 accounts.
claims.quote: An account gives a Copilot Studio agent its own identity in Microsoft 365 so it can take a business process from start to finish on its own.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Protected documents; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Agents with accounts cannot read protected documents, including Confidential or Internal Only protected documents.
claims.quote: Agents with an account can't read protected documents. For example, they can't access documents protected with Confidential or Internal Only sensitivity labels, or the equivalent for your organization.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Shared memory; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent keeps one shared memory across everyone it works with.
claims.quote: In an agent with its own account, that memory is shared. The agent keeps one memory across everyone it works with, so what one person explains benefits the whole team.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Shared memory; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Shared memory has no privacy boundary between users.
claims.quote: The agent is guided not to bring up one person's details with someone else, but shared memory has no privacy boundary between users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Shared memory; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The People card warns that shared file or chat summaries can appear in responses to users without source permissions.
claims.quote: The agent's People card displays this notice: "Any files or chats you share can be summarized and included in the agent's responses to any user, even users without permissions to the files or chats and regardless of sensitivity label."

claims.where: Risk assessment: Shared memory; Protected documents
claims.claim: The shared-memory warning applies regardless of sensitivity label, including content shared in chats.
claims.quote: Any files or chats you share can be summarized and included in the agent's responses to any user, even users without permissions to the files or chats and regardless of sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Shared memories are automatically deleted after 28 days without interaction.
claims.quote: If no one interacts with the agent for 28 days, the system automatically deletes its shared memories.

claims.claim: End users cannot opt out of shared memory in this preview.
claims.quote: No. End users can't opt out of shared memory in this preview. By using the agent, you consent to its use of shared memory.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio also creates a separate Microsoft Entra Agent ID for each agent with an account.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio also creates a Microsoft Entra Agent ID that admins manage separately, for each agent that has an account.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Admins manage the Microsoft Entra Agent ID separately in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically creates a Microsoft Entra Agent ID for each new agent you create. You can view and manage these identities in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

claims.claim: An agent with an account has two identity objects: its Entra account and its separate Entra Agent ID.
claims.quote: The agent has its own Microsoft Entra account and identity ... Copilot Studio also creates a Microsoft Entra Agent ID that admins manage separately, for each agent that has an account.

claims.claim: An agent account does not automatically grant every tool permission.
claims.quote: The agent account does not automatically grant every tool permission. Check which identity a tool uses and grant only the access needed for the job.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance

claims.quote: The agent's email address uses your own alias as a fixed prefix ... During this preview, you can't change the maker-based alias prefix or reporting relationship.

claims.claim: The agent reports to its maker.
claims.quote: The agent's email address uses your own alias as a fixed prefix, and the agent reports to you.

claims.claim: The maker-based reporting relationship cannot be changed during the preview.
claims.quote: During this preview, you can't change the maker-based alias prefix or reporting relationship.

claims.claim: Agents with an account can run from configured triggers.
claims.quote: Configure supported tools and a recurrence trigger; instructions alone don't create a schedule or grant access.

claims.claim: Agents with accounts can generate new documents.
claims.quote: Document editing: generating new documents is supported; editing existing documents through co-authoring isn't supported yet.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio data policies can restrict Power Platform connectors used as agent tools.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope. ... To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.claim: Data policies can restrict the documented supported capabilities of Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: Require user authentication; Block using Power Platform connectors as tools; Block HTTP requests; Block Azure Bot Service skills; Block publishing to specific channels; Block event triggers

claims.claim: Policies with a tenant scope apply to all agents in all environments across the tenant.
claims.quote: Policies with a tenant scope apply to all agents in all environments across the tenant.

claims.claim: The described tenant-scoped connector and capability policies are not a universal per-account action allow-list.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope. ... In the Power Platform admin center, you can classify Copilot Studio connectors within a data policy under the following data groups: Business; Non-business; Blocked

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Publishing fails when no Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates license is available.
claims.quote: If no Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates license is available in your tenant when you publish, publishing fails.

claims.claim: In the EEA the agent appears in Teams only if the tenant separately licenses Teams.
claims.quote: Your agent still gets its account, mailbox, and directory presence, but it appears in Microsoft Teams only if your tenant separately licenses Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: One documented maker licensing option is Microsoft 365 E5 with the Microsoft Agent 365 add-on.
claims.quote: You have a maker license: a Microsoft 365 E5 license with the Microsoft Agent 365 add-on, or a Microsoft 365 E7 license, which includes Agent 365.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The alternative documented maker license is Microsoft 365 E7, which includes Agent 365.
claims.quote: You have a maker license: a Microsoft 365 E5 license with the Microsoft Agent 365 add-on, or a Microsoft 365 E7 license, which includes Agent 365.

claims.claim: The tenant must be enrolled in Frontier with the Agent 365 Terms of Service accepted.
claims.quote: Your tenant is enrolled in the Microsoft Frontier Program, with the Microsoft Agent 365 Terms of Service accepted, and has Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates licenses available.

claims.where: summary; front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.claim: The agent uses its Frontier for AI Teammates license when the maker publishes.
claims.quote: Your agent uses one of these licenses for its account when you publish it.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An admin can remove a license from another agent to return it to the available pool.
claims.quote: If none are free when you publish, an admin must return a license to the pool by removing it from another agent, or acquire more.

claims.claim: Acquiring more licenses is another documented remedy for a depleted license pool.
claims.quote: Ask your admin to free up a license by removing it from another agent, or to acquire more licenses, and then publish again.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 Frontier page requires at least one Microsoft E7 license in the tenant to access Agent 365 preview features.
claims.quote: To access Agent 365 preview features in the Frontier program, your tenant must have at least one license of Microsoft E7.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: Account licensing and usage-based service charges are separate.

claims.claim: Using, building, testing and evaluating agents on this harness might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature page gives no price for the Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates license.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates" price licensing agent accounts general availability. Opened authoring-agent-account and microsoft-agent-365/frontier; neither publishes that license's price.

claims.claim: After enrollment the Frontier page tells admins to confirm 25 active Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates licenses.
claims.quote: Next, navigate to Billing > Licenses and confirm you see 25 active licenses for Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates.

claims.claim: The Frontier page describes generally available Agent 365 as licensed per user.

claims.claim: The agent-accounts feature page does not state its general-availability account licensing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates" price licensing agent accounts general availability. Opened authoring-agent-account and microsoft-agent-365/frontier; the feature page describes Frontier account licenses, not final account licensing.

claims.claim: Only users selected in template activation and members of selected groups can create agents with accounts.
claims.quote: Only the users you select at this step and members of the selected groups can create agents with accounts.

claims.claim: The environment must use the early release cycle.
claims.quote: Your environment uses the early release cycle. In the Power Platform admin center, verify that Release cycle for your environment is Early.

claims.claim: Agent accounts are available to customers in the European Economic Area.
claims.quote: Agent accounts are available to customers in the European Economic Area (EEA).

claims.claim: A tenant admin activates the Copilot Studio template.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, a tenant admin goes to All Agents, filters by Agent template: Yes, selects Copilot Studio (Frontier), and then selects Activate.

claims.claim: A global admin enrolls the tenant in Agent 365 Frontier.
claims.quote: Only a global admin for the tenant can enable Agent 365 Frontier, and the preview disclaimers in your customer agreements apply.

claims.claim: The Frontier enrollment path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Overview > Try now > I agree.
claims.quote: In Microsoft 365 admin center, navigate to Agents > Overview and select Try now in the banner and I agree to the Terms of Service.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn names no roles for the Power Platform admin center step.
claims.quote: To help you administer environments and settings for the Microsoft Power Platform, you can assign users to manage the service at the tenant level ... Power Platform administrator ... Perform admin functions in Microsoft Power Platform
claims.fix: Remove the sentence 'Learn names no roles for the Power Platform admin center step.' Microsoft documents general Power Platform service administration roles at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/use-service-admin-role-manage-tenant; the absence must not be stated about all of Learn.

claims.claim: Template activation is at All Agents > filter Agent template: Yes > Copilot Studio (Frontier) > Activate > Users step in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: a tenant admin goes to All Agents, filters by Agent template: Yes, selects Copilot Studio (Frontier), and then selects Activate. ... In the activation wizard, at the Users step, select the users or groups that can create agents with accounts

claims.claim: The template activation operation is POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/activate.
claims.quote: Activate an already-onboarded agent template for the users or groups allowed to create instances from it ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/activate

claims.claim: The documented activation and block APIs are beta APIs not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Activation is a reviewed beta contract whose deployed availability depends on the matching schema and backend release.
claims.quote: This reference describes the reviewed beta contract. Availability depends on the matching schema and backend release; API-review approval isn't evidence of deployed availability.

claims.claim: The activation and block Package Management API operations require a Microsoft Agent 365 license.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The activation and block operations use delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: | Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available. |

claims.claim: The reviewed native activation implementation requires a signed-in Global Administrator or AI Administrator.
claims.quote: The reviewed native implementation requires a signed-in Global Administrator or AI Administrator and the matching tenant feature admission.

claims.claim: The activation body uses agentManagerScope to select users or groups allowed to create template instances.
claims.quote: agentManagerScope ... Required. The users or groups allowed to create instances from this template. It isn't an installation audience or the recipients of an individual approval request.

claims.claim: packageVersion is a required activation request-body parameter.
claims.quote: packageVersion | String | Required. Version used for the versioned package preview, in `major.minor[.build[.revision]]` form.

claims.claim: policyTemplateId is a required activation request-body parameter.
claims.quote: policyTemplateId | String | Required. Opaque identifier of an existing policy template resolved by the service, not a policy-definition object.

claims.claim: The environment Agent accounts control is at Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Copilot Studio > Agent accounts.
claims.quote: select Copilot on the side bar, and then select Settings. ... Under Copilot Studio, select Agent accounts and turn on the setting for your environment.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or Power Platform API operation for the environment Agent accounts setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent accounts" "API" "setting"; "Agent accounts" "PowerShell" "environment"; "agent accounts" Dataverse organization table environment settings API enable. Opened authoring-agent-account and pac copilot-studio; searched Organization reference. No matching control.

claims.claim: Turning Agent accounts off hides the Agent account button for agents in that environment.
claims.quote: If you turn it off, the Agent account button isn't available for agents in the environment.

claims.claim: An agent is blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > select an agent > Block > Block agent > Save.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... select Block or Unblock. ... select either Block agent or Unblock agent, and then select Save.

claims.claim: The Graph block operation is POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Blocking Copilot Studio agents affects availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot and host products such as Outlook and Teams.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products, such as Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center uses the same controls for agent blocking as for other apps.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: No independent admin UI or API control to turn off shared memory for agents with accounts is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent accounts shared memory turn off independently admin Graph API PowerShell. Opened faq-agent-accounts and authoring-agent-account; FAQ requires turning off accounts altogether. The search's Memory toggle result concerns personal memory, not shared account memory.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].note; controls[3].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: In the preview admins must turn off agent accounts altogether to turn off shared memory.
claims.quote: No. In this preview, shared memory can't be turned off independently of agent accounts. To turn off shared memory, an admin must turn off agent accounts altogether.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in: both template activation and the environment Agent accounts setting are required before users can create agents with accounts.
claims.quote: Before users can create agents with accounts, admins must complete both steps in the following sections, in order.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, with account licensing and separate usage-based charges.
claims.quote: An agent account requires a Microsoft 365 Frontier for AI Teammates license and tenant Frontier enrollment, as described in Prerequisites. Account licensing and usage-based service charges are separate.

claims.claim: Cost is variable because the harness uses usage-based billing measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Anyone who talks to the agent participates in its shared-memory experience.
claims.quote: No. End users can't opt out of shared memory in this preview. By using the agent, you consent to its use of shared memory.
